title: Causal inference to scope environmental impact assessment of renewable energy projects
authors: Gazar H, Borsuk M, Calder M
abstract_text: Environmental impact assessment (EIA), life cycle analysis (LCA), and cost benefit analysis (CBA) embed crucial but subjective judgments over the extent of system boundaries and the range of impacts to consider as causally connected to an intervention, decision, or technology
intervention_meaning: In environmental science, 'intervention' means policy/technology deployment (e.g., renewable energy project) whose causal environmental impact is assessed

title: Unilateral climate policies can substantially reduce national carbon pollution
abstract_text: Following the failure of climate governance regimes that sought to impose legally binding treaty-based obligations, the Paris Agreement relies on voluntary actions by individual countries. Yet, there is no guarantee that unilateral policies will lead to a decrease in carbon emissions.
intervention_meaning: In climate policy, 'intervention' means unilateral national climate policies (e.g., carbon pricing) whose causal effect on emissions is evaluated

title: Identifying instrumental variables for causal inference
intervention_meaning: In finance, 'intervention' means policy/market interventions whose causal effect on financial outcomes is identified via instrumental variables

title: Inference in Nonparametric Instrumental Variables With Partial Identification
intervention_meaning: In finance/economics, 'intervention' refers to policy changes whose causal effects are partially identified through IV methods

title: Best practices for moving from correlation to causation in ecological research
authors: Correia N, Dee L, Byrnes J
abstract_text: In ecology, causal questions are ubiquitous, yet the literature describing systematic approaches to answering these questions is vast and fragmented across different traditions (e.g., randomization, structural equation modeling, convergent cross mapping).
intervention_meaning: In ecology, 'intervention' means ecological management actions (e.g., habitat restoration, species removal) whose causal effects on ecosystems are assessed

title: Improving causal inference from unreplicated on-farm strip trials with propensity scores
abstract_text: Farmers often conduct unreplicated on-farm experiments (OFE) to evaluate management practices such as the application of plant growth regulators (PGR) in winter wheat.
intervention_meaning: In agricultural science, 'intervention' means management practices (e.g., fertilizer, PGR application) whose causal effect on crop yield is evaluated through on-farm trials
